components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Compact primary action using Ledger Ink and a visible focus ring.
components.css: .ds-button-primary { height: 2rem; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius, 0.625rem); background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); font: 500 0.875rem/1 'Geist Variable', sans-serif; transition: background-color 180ms ease-out, transform 180ms ease-out, box-shadow 180ms ease-out; } .ds-button-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary), var(--background) 15%); } .ds-button-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring), transparent 50%); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action for adjacent but lower-priority operations.
components.css: .ds-button-outline { height: 2rem; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius, 0.625rem); background: var(--background); color: var(--foreground); font: 500 0.875rem/1 'Geist Variable', sans-serif; transition: background-color 180ms ease-out, color 180ms ease-out, box-shadow 180ms ease-out; } .ds-button-outline:hover { background: var(--muted); } .ds-button-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring), transparent 50%); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Compact field with tokenized border, readable placeholder, and strong focus treatment.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 2rem; min-width: 0; border: 1px solid var(--input); border-radius: var(--radius, 0.625rem); background: transparent; color: var(--foreground); padding: 0.25rem 0.625rem; font: 400 0.875rem/1.4 'Geist Variable', sans-serif; transition: border-color 180ms ease-out, box-shadow 180ms ease-out; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground); opacity: 1; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ring), transparent 50%); } .ds-input[aria-invalid='true'] { border-color: var(--destructive); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklch, var(--destructive), transparent 80%); }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Small state label that pairs tone with readable text; color is never the only cue.
components.css: .ds-status-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--border); background: var(--muted); color: var(--foreground); padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; font: 500 0.75rem/1.2 'Geist Variable', sans-serif; } .ds-status-badge::before { content: ''; width: 0.375rem; height: 0.375rem; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--primary); }

narrative.overview: Trackpal should feel like a calm operational ledger: clear enough for repeated daily work, stable enough for credential and subscription tasks, and quiet enough that WhatsApp, tenant, mailbox, and role boundaries stay legible. The current React frontend establishes a shadcn/base-nova foundation: Geist Variable, neutral OKLCH tokens, compact controls, rounded-lg buttons and inputs, rounded-xl cards, borders, muted fills, and visible focus rings. This system is product-first. Familiar controls are an asset. Future screens should look trustworthy to operators who manage tenants, clients, subscriptions, mailbox connections, and access-code workflows in Spanish-first contexts.
keyCharacteristics: Restrained neutral surfaces with near-black primary actions.
Comfortable and calm density: not sparse marketing, not cramped infrastructure UI.
Role-aware layouts where master, tenant, and client capabilities are unmistakable.
Bilingual-ready labels, forms, tables, and validation messages.
State vocabulary that uses text, shape, iconography, and tone rather than color alone.

rules.name: The ≤10% Ink Rule
rules.body: Primary ink is for action and selection. If a screen is mostly primary color, the hierarchy has failed.

rules.name: The No Decorative Accent Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce indigo, gradients, or arbitrary success colors as ornament. Every non-neutral color must represent state, risk, selection, or a documented data role.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Product UI uses Geist for everything until a real data-display need proves otherwise. No display fonts in controls, labels, tables, or form fields.

rules.name: The No Gradient Text Rule
rules.body: Gradient text is prohibited. Emphasis comes from hierarchy, not background-clip decoration.

rules.name: The Border-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Start with ring-foreground/10, border-border, muted footers, and spacing. Add shadow only when a surface must float above another surface.

rules.name: The State-Only Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion is 150–250ms and explains state: hover, focus, loading, expansion, or route feedback. No choreographed page-load sequences.

dos: Do preserve the shadcn/base-nova token system in frontend/src/index.css; extend tokens there instead of scattering raw colors.
Do keep product screens comfortable and calm: compact enough for repeat operators, spacious enough for Spanish labels and validation text.
Do make role boundaries obvious through navigation, copy, permissions, and page structure.
Do use visible focus rings, keyboard-reachable controls, and non-color-only status cues.
Do use cards only when they clarify containment; tables, panels, sections, and inline flows are often better for operational work.
donts: Don't use generic SaaS-card aesthetics: gradient hero text, repeated metric-card scaffolds, decorative dashboards, startup-template polish, or visual effects that do not improve operator confidence.
Don't use background-clip: text gradients. The current scaffold pattern should be removed, not expanded.
Don't add colored side-stripe borders, glassmorphism, decorative blur cards, or arbitrary high z-index values.
Don't use muted gray for required labels, important data, or core body copy.
Don't hardcode raw Tailwind colors for component variants when semantic tokens or installed shadcn variants exist.
